sources.title: Large Language Model Hacking: Quantifying the Hidden Risks of Using LLMs for Text Annotation
quotations: configuration choices lead to incorrect conclusions
incorrect conclusions in approximately 31% of hypotheses for state-of-the-art LLMs
human annotations provide crucial protection against false positives
sources.what_it_is_used_for: Context and a named failure mode. Their setting is statistical inference over annotated corpora; ours is adjudication of a rule's verdicts against a text in front of the reader. The transfer is not automatic and nothing here rests on their 31%.

sources.title: What Is Actually Being Annotated? Inter-Prompt Reliability as a Measurement Problem in LLM-Based Social Science Labeling
quotations: LLM annotation exhibits substantial stochastic variation in interpretative tasks, while appearing more stable in knowledge-based tasks
majority voting across prompts significantly improves reproducibility and reduces variance
sources.what_it_is_used_for: The reason this session uses four workers and a majority rather than one worker, and the reason its predictions expect stability: the document is in front of the reader, which puts this task nearer the knowledge-anchored kind than the interpretative one.

sources.title: To Err Is Human; To Annotate, SILICON? Toward Robust Reproducibility in LLM Annotation
quotations: baseline-induced error from unreliable human references
sources.what_it_is_used_for: Names the error source this session is the limit case of: there is no human reference here at all, reliable or otherwise.
